question: How should generative-model science identify stable explanatory regularities when architectures, APIs, and benchmark capabilities change faster than bottom-up theories?

key_findings.claim: The paper argues that benchmark scores sit too high in the explanatory hierarchy to reveal the strategies that produce them.
key_findings.evidence: A fictional high-performing but architecturally alien 'Newformer' illustrates that task scores alone would not say whether it copies, follows demonstrations, or uses the same sub-behaviors as transformers. The authors propose behavior categories between benchmarks/skills and learned mechanisms/elements.

key_findings.claim: A behavior is framed as a model-agnostic metamodel that predicts limited output features under an explicit input and randomness distribution.
key_findings.evidence: For generator M:X×R→Y, a behavior B:X→F is explanatory insofar as B(X) reduces uncertainty about M(X,R). Mutual information quantifies coverage; an MDL-style objective trades the code length of B against conditional output entropy to discourage a behavior that merely reproduces the model.

key_findings.claim: Behavior discovery should precede and generate benchmarks rather than be reduced to adding more benchmark tasks.
key_findings.evidence: The authors distinguish discovering a tendency such as prompting/copying from measuring performance in a fixed context. They argue behaviors form reusable factors whose Cartesian products with tasks expose failure modes and guide mechanistic hypotheses.

key_findings.claim: Calling generative models complex systems is primarily a research-program analogy, not an empirically validated new theory.
key_findings.evidence: The paper defines emergence as macro-level regularity hard to predict from known micro-dynamics and contrasts engineered RNN copying with transformer copying that emerged from general training. It offers no criterion for when unpredictability, scale, or interaction complexity crosses into a distinct complex-systems regime.

key_findings.claim: Open weights and artifacts are essential to the proposed science because they preserve the unusual experimental advantages of artificial systems.
key_findings.evidence: The authors enumerate perfect state recording, known low-level transitions, exact repeatability, reversible perturbation, lack of observer effects, and human-legible outputs. Proprietary drifting APIs undermine most of these advantages through hidden updates, unavailable internal interventions, and unknown auxiliary behavior.

anchors.section: 4 A different kind of complex system

method.core_idea: Build an architecture-agnostic, hierarchical vocabulary of observable generative behaviors that compresses and predicts outputs across tasks, then use it to guide benchmarks and mechanistic explanation.
method.mechanism: Use thought experiments and examples from copying, prompting, repetition, memorization, translation failure, and image generation to separate benchmark, skill, behavior, learned structure, element, and mathematical model levels. Formalize candidate behaviors through mutual information and minimum description length under stated distributions, and motivate systematic black-box perturbation of fully archived open models.
assumptions: Cross-task behavioral regularities can be discovered and named at a stable level independent of architecture.
Useful behaviors admit operational feature maps and input distributions for estimating explanatory information.
Description length of a behavioral rule is sufficiently well defined to compare explanations.
Human inspection plus controlled experiments can discover behaviors missed by anticipated benchmarks.
Open-model capability lag is small enough that behavior discovered there transfers to frontier systems.

techniques.role: Stress-tests whether an analysis method survives radical architecture change.
Links benchmarks and skills through behaviors to learned structure and low-level components.
Quantifies output uncertainty reduced by a behavioral predictor under a distribution.
Balances explanatory coverage against complexity of the behavior description.
Separates shared, contingent, idiosyncratic, and unexpressed patterns across corpus and generations.
Uses repeatable storage and reversible interventions to study artificial complex systems.

limitations: This is a perspective/position paper with no implemented taxonomy, behavior-discovery algorithm, dataset, benchmark, metamodel, or empirical test of the formal objective.
Behavior boundaries are observer- and vocabulary-dependent; the paper does not specify annotation reliability, granularity selection, or ontology revision rules.
Mutual information with enormous structured output spaces is intractable without lossy features, while MDL depends on coding language and can favor spurious but compressive correlations.
The complex-systems analogy does not yield distinctive falsifiable predictions beyond existing behavioral evaluation and interpretability agendas.
Black-box behavior can be prompt-, decoding-, version-, language-, and deployment-distribution-specific, undermining stable categories.
Human-legible outputs invite anthropomorphic categorization and experimenter 'tells,' which the authors acknowledge but do not operationally control.
The argument selectively samples a vast literature and explicitly disclaims survey completeness.
failure_modes: A named behavior groups superficially similar outputs produced by unrelated mechanisms and fails to transfer across contexts.
Taxonomies proliferate into benchmark-like one-off labels rather than parsimonious reusable factors.
A metamodel predicts outputs well from dataset artifacts but provides no causal or actionable explanation.
Provider updates or decoding nondeterminism make an apparent behavioral law irreproducible.
Open models differ systematically from closed frontier systems, so discovered behavior does not transfer.
MDL rewards an opaque learned surrogate that compresses outputs but is no more understandable than the primary model.
reusable_insights: Ask whether an interpretability claim would remain meaningful for a functionally similar model with a different architecture.
Separate discovering a behavior, characterizing its boundary conditions, measuring it in benchmarks, and locating its mechanism.
State the prompt/input and randomness distribution whenever claiming a model tendency.
Prefer behavior factors that predict outcomes across multiple tasks and generate targeted counterfactual evaluations.
Archive weights, code, data, seeds, decoding settings, and intermediate states so behavioral experiments remain exactly repeatable.
open_questions: How can behavior ontologies be induced, merged, and validated with inter-rater and cross-model reliability?
Which estimators make behavior coverage and MDL tractable for open-ended text, images, audio, and interactive agents?
Can behavioral metamodels predict novel task failures better than benchmark aggregates and scaling curves?
What experimental evidence would falsify the complex-systems framing or distinguish it from ordinary system identification?
How should causal mechanisms be linked to behavior categories when redundant circuits or multiple architectures implement the same tendency?

competitive_landscape.title: Language Model Behavior: A Comprehensive Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Chang and Bergen synthesize more than 250 studies into empirical capability and failure categories. Holtzman et al. instead argue for a future architecture-independent taxonomy and an information-theoretic criterion, but do not instantiate it.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
competitive_landscape.difference: CheckList operationalizes behavioral testing with capabilities, invariance, and directional-expectation test types. The target perspective calls for broader discovered cross-task behaviors and metamodels rather than expert-authored capability matrices alone.

competitive_landscape.title: Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: BIG-bench coordinates hundreds of diverse tasks and studies capability scaling. This paper argues such breadth still cannot discover or explain shared behavioral strategies and should be downstream of behavioral decomposition.

competitive_landscape.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: HELM standardizes scenarios, metrics, and transparency for broad model comparison. Behavioral complex-systems science targets reusable explanatory regularities beneath scenario performance; the two agendas are complementary.

competitive_landscape.title: Emergent Abilities of Large Language Models
competitive_landscape.difference: Wei et al. catalog benchmark abilities that appear abruptly with scale. The target paper shifts attention from ability scores to output strategies and warns that discovery and explanation require a vocabulary below the benchmark level.

novelty_assessment.author_claim: The authors claim generative modeling has become a complex-systems science and propose behavior taxonomy/metamodel discovery as the missing layer between benchmarks and mechanisms.
novelty_assessment.evidence: Sections 1-4 develop the Newformer stress test, explanatory hierarchy, information-theoretic behavior definition, benchmark critique, emergence analogy, and open-model advantages.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Behavioral testing, capability taxonomies, emergent-ability catalogs, MDL explanations, and holistic evaluation all predate the paper. Its distinctive contribution is a clear synthesis: architecture-proof behavioral regularities should be treated as explanatory objects and benchmark building blocks. The value is agenda-setting, not demonstrated methodology.

reviewer_notes: Read all 22 cached pages, including the mutual-information/MDL formalism, training-inference mapping, open-versus-API caveats, thought experiments, and explicit limitations. Primary arXiv predecessors spanning behavioral surveys/testing, BIG-bench, HELM, and emergence were checked on 2026-08-23. No empirical results are invented for this position paper.
